Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

blorr (development version)

Supported inputs and precision

  • The data-column functions (blr_segment(), blr_segment_dist(), blr_segment_twoway(), blr_woe_iv(), blr_woe_iv_stats() and blr_bivariate_analysis()) support one or two observed, non-missing response levels. Supported encodings are numeric 0/1, logical, factor and character; the event is the second level, TRUE or 1. A single observed level returns the defined rate (all 0 or all 1), and a level labelled "1" or TRUE is the event, so numeric and factor encodings agree. Unused factor levels and rows with a missing response are ignored. Numeric codes other than 0/1 are not supported. Segment and two-way functions keep a missing predictor as its own NA level; WoE/IV excludes rows with a missing response or predictor. Empty input is an error because it has no response levels.
  • Proportions are returned unrounded. Segment tables print percentages to two decimal places, two-way rates to three decimal places, WoE/IV components to digits decimal places, and the total information value is rounded once at print time. Plots use the unrounded proportions.

Behaviour changes

  • blr_segment_twoway() now reports the event rate within each pair of levels: events in a cyl x gear cell divided by the non-missing responses in that cell. Versions up to 0.3.2 divided the event counts of each cell by all non-missing responses in the sample (the share of all observations), which understated every rate. For am, cyl and gear in mtcars, the cyl 4 / gear 4 cell is now 0.750 (6 events out of 8 observations) instead of 0.188 (6 out of 32). A cell with no non-missing responses is NA and prints as -.

  • blr_segment() and blr_segment_dist() now return unrounded proportions in 1s% and n% and round only when printing. Versions up to 0.3.2 rounded the proportions to two decimal places before multiplying by 100, so the printed percentages and the plot used false precision: for am by cyl in mtcars, cyl 4 is now 34.38% of the sample and has a 72.73% event rate, instead of printing 34.00% and 73.00% from the stored 0.34 and 0.73. The plot of blr_segment_dist() now uses the unrounded proportions.

  • A response with one observed level is accepted again by the data-column functions and returns the defined empirical rates: 0 when every response is a non-event and 1 when every response is an event. blr_woe_iv() and blr_woe_iv_stats() apply the documented 0.5 continuity correction to the zero cells, so their corrected within-class distributions are equal and WoE and IV are 0. A factor whose only level is "1" or TRUE is now all events, the same as numeric 1, so the earlier numeric/factor disagreement is fixed. A response with no observed level remains an error, and the model APIs that need two classes still reject a one-level response.

Bug fixes

  • A response with more than two levels is now rejected with an error naming the response and the number of levels found. glm() silently recodes a factor response with three or more levels as “first level” versus “everything else”, so a three-level response was fitted without complaint. A character response such as as.character(hsb2$ses) instead fails in glm() with “y values must be 0 <= y <= 1”. For glm(ses ~ female + read, hsb2, family = binomial()) the three-level ses response was fitted and the summary printed by blr_regress() reported 47 and 95 of 200 observations, silently dropping the third level (58). Every model entry point now raises this error: blr_regress(), blr_model_fit_stats(), the blr_rsq_*() functions, the stepwise functions, blr_gains_table(), blr_confusion_matrix() and blr_test_hosmer_lemeshow(). Binary responses are unchanged.

  • A response with a single outcome is rejected by blr_regress() with `y` has 1 level; blorr needs both events and non-events. because its response summary prints the two outcomes side by side. The model diagnostics accept a degenerate single-outcome fit again, as they did before the one-level check was added: blr_confusion_matrix() reports the defined counts (for glm(rep(0, 32) ~ wt, mtcars, family = binomial()), 32 true zeroes and accuracy 1) and marks the undefined statistics NA, and blr_model_fit_stats(), the blr_rsq_*() functions, blr_gains_table() and blr_test_hosmer_lemeshow() run on it again.

  • blr_woe_iv(), blr_woe_iv_stats(), blr_segment(), blr_segment_dist() and blr_segment_twoway() now use the same error for response columns with more than two observed, non-missing levels, instead of silently treating the second level as the event. Numeric 0/1, two-level factor, logical and two-value character responses are unchanged; unused factor levels are ignored.

  • An explicit missing factor response (factor(..., exclude = NULL)) is now excluded from the data-column functions like any other missing response. Previously is.na() did not detect the explicit missing level, so the row was counted as a non-event: for y = factor(c("0", "1", NA, "0", "1"), exclude = NULL) grouped by g, the a group had n = 3 and one event instead of n = 2 and one event, and WoE/IV counted two non-events instead of one. The event is also the second non-missing level when a factor carries an explicit missing level.

  • blr_woe_iv() and blr_woe_iv_stats() keep the event class of the original response when rows with a missing predictor are removed. Previously a factor response whose non-event class disappeared with those rows was re-levelled and its remaining event class became the non-event class; numeric 0/1 responses already gave the correct counts. Both encodings now agree.

  • blr_woe_iv() and blr_woe_iv_stats() now stop with a named complete-case error when no complete observations remain. Previously a two-class response with an all-missing predictor produced an empty table and printed Information Value 0, which read as zero information rather than no evidence.

  • The association table in the blr_regress() output now prints % Concordant, % Discordant and % Tied on the percentage scale, keeping the % labels: for am ~ wt + hp on mtcars it shows 98.3806, 1.6194 and 0.0000. Versions up to 0.3.2 printed the proportions 0.9838, 0.0162 and 0.0000 under the same labels. The n% and 1s% columns printed by blr_segment() and blr_segment_dist() follow the same convention; their returned proportions are now unrounded (see Behaviour changes).

  • The total information value printed by blr_woe_iv() and blr_woe_iv_stats() is now computed from the unrounded information value components and rounded once for printing, instead of summing components that had already been rounded to digits. For the two-level example with digits = 1 the total is now 0.5 rather than 0.4. blr_bivariate_analysis() likewise uses the unrounded total.

  • blr_segment(), blr_segment_dist() and blr_segment_twoway() keep a missing predictor as its own NA level instead of failing inside the width calculation of the printer. The NA rows get their own count, sample share and event rate, and print with an NA label. Rows with a missing response are still excluded first. The two-way function keeps the within-cell rate fix and adds an NA row or column for a missing grouping value.

  • The blr_segment_twoway() printer now handles a table with no rows or no columns without failing in max() or rep(). A no-event cell in a non-empty table shows a zero rate, and an empty cell shows -.

  • blr_segment_dist() now prints the predictor’s factor levels (for blr_segment_dist(mtcarz, am, cyl), 4, 6 and 8 instead of the integer codes 1, 2 and 3) and the predictor’s name as the column header (cyl instead of the internal pred); the same name is used as the plot title. blr_segment_twoway() now prints the two grouping variables as its headers (gear across the top and cyl down the left) instead of the response and the first predictor. Earlier versions printed am and cyl for blr_segment_twoway(mtcarz, am, cyl, gear).

  • blr_residual_diagnostics() now computes the delta deviance (difdev) as the squared deviance residual plus CBAR. Versions up to and including 0.3.2 used the squared standardized Pearson residual instead, so their difdev values were wrong (for glm(am ~ wt + hp, mtcars, family = binomial()) the first three were 0.272, 2.398 and 0.036 instead of 0.385, 2.273 and 0.063). blr_plot_diag_difdev(), blr_plot_difdev_fitted(), blr_plot_difdev_leverage() and blr_plot_diag_influence() show the corrected values.

blorr 0.3.2

CRAN release: 2026-11-16

This is a patch release that fixes several bugs in model fit statistics, variable selection, bivariate analysis, model validation, gains tables, weight of evidence, and the Gini index.

Bug Fixes

  • blr_regress() now summarises the fitted model directly, so an offset supplied in the model formula and the formula environment are respected.
  • The intercept-only null model used in model fit statistics and likelihood ratio tests retains the fitted model’s response, offset and family/link, and is not confused by data columns named weights or offset.
  • Package attachment no longer accesses the network to check for updates.
  • Cox-Snell and Nagelkerke R2 now use the number of observations the model was fitted on, so they are correct when rows are dropped for missing values or when the model is fitted without a data argument. The model fit statistics table is also assembled by name, so values no longer shift between labels.
  • blr_vif_tol() now identifies the intercept from the fitted terms instead of assuming the first design column, so a model without an intercept reports tolerance and VIF for every predictor instead of silently dropping one.
  • blr_model_fit_stats() no longer reports a zero likelihood ratio test for a model without an intercept. The intercept-only model is only used as the null when it is actually nested in the fitted design; otherwise the test is reported as unavailable with a warning.
  • The likelihood ratio test now checks nesting structurally: the reduced model’s estimated terms must be a subset, by name and values, of the full model’s, with the same response, rows, weights and offset. The columns must be identical (compared exactly, with no tolerance), so a comparison that cannot be established as nested stops with an error instead of returning chi-square inference. Equivalent parameterizations under different names (other factor contrasts, I(wt) for wt) are not recognised as nested.
  • The model overview now prints Df. Model as the number of estimated coefficients excluding the intercept, instead of the null residual df.
  • The stepwise p-value (both directions) summary now labels its last column Deviance, which is what it reports, instead of C(p).
  • Weighted and grouped binomial models are not supported: every function that takes a model now stops with “blorr supports unweighted 0/1 (Bernoulli) models; weighted and grouped binomial models are not supported.” This covers any prior weight other than 1 (zero weights included), a cbind(successes, failures) response and proportion responses. Fits stored without their model frame or response (model = FALSE, y = FALSE) are declined with a request to refit with model = TRUE, y = TRUE. The response name in the overview is printed as one expression.
  • Only binary logistic regression models (binomial family with logit link) are supported. All model entry points reject other links and families, including quasibinomial, with a clear error; selection rejects them before refitting.
  • The AIC selection detail tables print the real degrees of freedom of each term (for example 3 for a four-level factor) instead of 1.
  • blr_regress() works for a model with no coefficients, and the p-value selection procedures stop with a clear message for a model with aliased terms instead of failing with an obscure error.
  • blr_step_aic_backward() now takes the first row (AIC, BIC and deviance) from the same refitted full model that every removal is compared with, so a model fitted without an intercept no longer produces a mixed baseline row or a wrong first removal.
  • The likelihood ratio test now uses the difference in residual degrees of freedom between the reduced and full models, giving the correct degrees of freedom and p-value for nested models.
  • Multi-model fit statistics are now labeled by name, so each measure is shown against the correct model statistic.
  • The event rate reported by blr_segment() and blr_segment_dist() is now the share of events within each level rather than the share of all events, and no longer fails when a level has no events.
  • blr_regress() now reports the number of observations and the response profile from the data used to fit the model when rows are dropped for missing values, including for factor responses whose levels are not 0 and 1.
  • Forward selection now stores the BIC and deviance of each step instead of the AIC after the first step.
  • Variable selection now adds or removes exactly one term per step when candidate p values or AIC values tie. The printed step history, AIC and the other per-step values are no longer mislabelled or shifted when several candidates share a p value (which can underflow to 0 on large data): p-value ties are broken by the Wald chi-square statistic and AIC ties by candidate order.
  • Variance decomposition proportions in blr_eigen_cindex() now sum to one for each coefficient. Eigenvalues and condition indices are now computed from the singular values of the scaled design rather than from its cross-product, so a nearly collinear full-rank design keeps a finite index and a design without an intercept keeps its predictor names.
  • Somers’ D and Goodman-Kruskal gamma in blr_pairs() now use the correct denominators.
  • Gains tables now assign every observation to exactly one of ten deciles, count events using the event level of the response, and no longer fail for small samples or when a decile contains only one outcome.
  • Gains tables and Lorenz data now assign deciles after dropping rows with missing outcomes or predictors, so those rows no longer cause an error or misaligned deciles.
  • Confusion matrices now show both outcome classes even when the model predicts only one class, McNemar’s test is reported as unavailable when it cannot be computed, and the no information rate uses the larger class.
  • The Gini index and Lorenz curve now use the observations the model was fitted on, so rows dropped for missing values are no longer misaligned, and the Gini index is reported as 2 * AUC - 1, the credit-scoring definition based on the area under the ROC curve (values differ from earlier versions, which reported the concentration index of the predicted probabilities). The index is computed from the Mann-Whitney rank statistic, so it remains fast on large models, and data without the response column is now an error.
  • The default blr_gini_index() call now uses the fitted response labels, so labelled factor and logical responses give the same index as an explicit data argument instead of NaN.
  • Variable selection procedures now return an intercept-only model when no predictor qualifies, and p-value based procedures apply the entry criterion to the first predictor as well.
  • Variable selection procedures now refit candidate models on the stored model frame, so predictors supplied as expressions such as log(wt) or built from locally defined functions are handled correctly, and editing or reassigning the source data after fitting no longer changes the selected terms. The returned model keeps the original term expressions, so predict() on raw new data recomputes terms such as log(wt) or poly(x, 2) as for an ordinary glm() fit, and interaction terms such as x:z and non-syntactic names such as `body weight` are refit correctly.
  • Models returned by variable selection keep formula and argument offsets exactly once in their model frame, so confint() and the odds ratio limits of blr_regress() match an ordinary glm() fit, and models fitted with na.action = na.exclude keep their padded residuals, fitted values and predictions.
  • blr_pairs(), and therefore blr_regress(), now works for models fitted with na.action = na.exclude.
  • Variable selection preserves the original formula and offsets, so predict() on new data uses the new offset values. If a selected model cannot be rebuilt exactly from the original terms, selection now stops with an error instead of returning a model whose predictions could differ from glm().
  • blr_regress() now matches standard errors, z values and p-values to the coefficients by name, so an aliased coefficient no longer shifts them onto other predictors; aliased rows show 0 degrees of freedom and missing statistics, and odds ratio tables with aliased coefficients now print.
  • Variable selection rebuilds selected terms from the fitted model’s own expressions, so terms with high-precision constants such as I(wt / 3.141592653589793) keep their exact values.
  • blr_regress(odd_conf_limit = TRUE) now works for intercept-only models, reporting an empty odds ratio table, and reports the odds ratio of every predictor of a model without an intercept.
  • Forward, backward and stepwise selection now keep the fitted model’s offset and contrasts in every candidate model, and print the same fitted model they return.
  • blr_woe_iv() now accepts character and numeric predictors, drops unused factor levels, applies a 0.5 continuity correction to levels with no events or no non-events, and drops rows with missing values so they are not counted as non-events.
  • blr_plot_dfbetas_panel() now works for models with one or more predictors.
  • Odds ratio confidence limits in blr_regress() are now labelled as profile-likelihood intervals.
  • The forward selection documentation now describes selection by AIC.
  • Deviance residual plots now use and are labelled as standardized deviance residuals.
  • Forward AIC selection now compares the best first candidate with the intercept-only model and returns the intercept-only model when no predictor improves AIC.
  • blr_regress() can summarise a fit whose response is a transformed expression.
  • Likelihood ratio tests reject models fitted to different observations, weights or offsets, or non-nested models, and bivariate analysis fits its null model on the predictor model’s complete rows. Nesting is checked against the fitted design matrices, including the intercept and the actual predictor values, and comparisons with no additional parameters are rejected.
  • Efron, count, adjusted count and McKelvey-Zavoina R-squared align fitted values with the fitted response when na.action = na.exclude.
  • Missing responses are no longer counted as non-events in segment, gains, confusion matrix and validation summaries, and unused response levels no longer change which class is treated as the event.
  • Validation functions now reject held-out response values that are not one of the two response classes the model was fitted on, instead of silently counting them as non-events.
  • The Hosmer-Lemeshow test accepts numeric and labelled factor responses and explicit data, uses degrees of freedom based on the observed number of groups, and reports the test as unavailable when too few groups remain.
  • Weight of evidence and information value are computed at full precision before being rounded, avoiding infinite values from small proportions.
  • blr_pairs() uses wide counters, so pair counts above the 32-bit integer limit no longer overflow.
  • Residual degrees of freedom are taken from the fitted rank, so aliased coefficients are not counted as estimated parameters.
  • Constant predictors now get infinite variance inflation factors and unavailable variance proportions, and blr_vif_tol() works for a single predictor.
  • Condition indices stay finite for full-rank designs with a small positive eigenvalue, and zero-variance predictor columns are handled without an error, reporting an infinite index and unavailable variance proportions.
  • The maintainer email address is now aravindhebbali@rsquaredacademy.com.
  • blr_prep_lorenz_data() defaults to the model frame and consistently uses the fitted rows for training data. Its example now calls the function with the default data argument instead of the non-existent model$data.
  • Executable selection and dfbetas examples now use the binomial family and the correct model class.
  • Likelihood ratio nesting checks now normalize the design columns before comparing column spaces, so rescaling a predictor no longer changes whether a no-intercept or non-nested comparison is accepted. Each column is scaled by its largest absolute value before its norm is taken, so very large or very small predictor values (for example of order 1e155 or 1e-200) no longer overflow or underflow and let a non-nested comparison through. The full column space now has the fitted model’s rank, so a nearly collinear direction the fit estimates is no longer dropped and a valid nested comparison is no longer rejected. When nesting cannot be confirmed to numerical precision the error says so. Nesting, and whether the intercept-only model is nested for blr_model_fit_stats(), is checked on the observations with positive prior weight using the fitted model’s non-aliased columns, so zero weights or zero-trial groups no longer cause valid nested comparisons to be rejected. The check compares the column spaces themselves, through orthonormal bases with a rounding tolerance based on the designs’ condition numbers, so adding a large constant to a predictor no longer lets a non-nested comparison through.

CRAN release: 2018-12-14

This is a minor release to fix bugs and for other enhancements.

Enhancements

  • variable selection procedures now return the final model as an object of class glm (#58)
  • data preparation functions of selected plots are now exported to enable end users to create customized plots and to use plotting library of their choice (#64)
  • informs users about new versions (#1)

Bug Fixes

  • tibble package breaking changes (#74)
